text:
lisa-customer: Hi, support — after a config change on our corporate load balancer, our apps get TLS handshake failures when talking to our Redwood Private endpoint. Only from corp network, public internet works. curl shows: "curl: (35) SSL: TLSv1.2 (UNKNOWN) alert handshake failure"

sam.dev: Thanks, lisa. Can you paste the full curl command you used and the openssl s_client output? Also which LB (F5, AWS ALB, etc.)?

lisa-customer: Using our on-prem F5. Command: `curl -v https://private.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"`
Openssl output (sanitized):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
139739286652384:error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure:ssl/s23_srvr.c:773:
---
No peer certificate available
---
SSL handshake has read 7 bytes and written 314 bytes
```

priya.platform: That error usually means the client and server couldn't agree on a cipher or protocol. Redwood supports TLS 1.2+ and prefers ECDHE RSA/AES-GCM ciphers. Does your F5 have older ciphers only (RC4/DES) or are ECDHE suites disabled?

lisa-customer: We recently tightened cipher policy to legacy suites for an older app, maybe we broke ECDHE. How can we confirm?

sam.dev: Quick checks: 1) run `openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.example.com:443 -tls1_2 -cipher ECDHE` and `-cipher DEFAULT` and compare. 2) capture a client-side `openssl s_client -msg -connect ...` to see ServerHello cipher list. Example command and expected line:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.example.com:443 -tls1_2 -cipher ECDHE
...
---
Cipher    : ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
```
If server never returns a certificate or returns an alert immediately, it's likely the LB is rejecting server's ServerHello or not allowing ECDHE groups.

nate-sre: Also check the F5 logs for TLS profile errors. On BIG-IP, iRules can force specific ciphers; check your SSL profile for `Cipher Group` settings. If the profile is set to a narrow legacy group (e.g., `DEFAULT:!ECDHE`), that would cause no shared cipher.

lisa-customer: Ran the openssl test. With `-cipher ECDHE` it times out/alerts. With `-cipher AES` I get a different server certificate presented but then app fails with 403 from our downstream auth. So looks like the LB is negotiating a non-ECDHE suite and then our downstream fails. Weird.

sam.dev: Redwood's server cert is RSA-based and supports ECDHE key exchange suites (ECDHE-RSA-*). If your LB is configured to do TLS termination and then re-initialize to backend, ensure it supports those key-exchange algorithms and TLS1.2+. If your LB rewrites SNI or strips ALPN, that can also cause issues with clients expecting HTTP/2.

priya.platform: Can you dump `openssl ciphers -v 'ALL:eNULL'` on the LB host to see enabled ciphers, or paste the F5 SSL profile name? If the profile contains `!ECDHE` or is older like `DEFAULT:!kEECDH`, that's the culprit.

lisa-customer: Profile name is `corp-ssl-legacy`. I see in config: `cipher group: HIGH:MEDIUM:!aNULL:!eNULL:!MD5`. Not obvious. Any quick remediation?

nate-sre: For F5, try switching to a modern profile temporarily (e.g., `modern-compat` or `DEFAULT:@SECLEVEL=2`) or add `ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384` at top of cipher list. Test on a single VIP to avoid wide blast.

lisa-customer: We tested adding ECDHE suites to the top of the list on a test VIP, and openssl now shows `Cipher : ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256`. But our app still saw intermittent `handshake failure` from some client subnets.

sam.dev: Could be middleboxes (corporate proxies) doing TLS inspection and presenting their own certs, or older clients that don't support ECDHE. For the intermittent case, capture a tcpdump from a failing client and compare to successful one. Check whether the failing clients are using ancient Java (<8u31) or old OpenSSL.

lisa-customer: tcpdump from a failing client shows `Alert (Level: Fatal, Description: handshake_failure)` immediately after ClientHello. ServerHello not present. That points to the LB rejecting the client's ClientHello.

priya.platform: Another angle: ensure the LB's list of supported curves includes prime256v1 and x25519 if possible. Some vendors require explicit enablement of EC curves. Without matching curves, ECDHE handshakes fail even if ciphers are enabled.

nate-sre: Good point. On F5: `tmm ssl profile` should show `ecdh curves`. Add `prime256v1` and `secp384r1`. Also ensure TLS versions include 1.2 and 1.3 if supported.

lisa-customer: Added curves and explicitly allowed ECDHE suites. Retested across clients — successful from all subnets now. Thanks!

sam.dev: Great. For the record, root cause: LB cipher/profile prevented ECDHE key exchange (missing ECDH curves and ordering), causing no shared cipher and immediate handshake failure. Action items we recommend to customers: 1) enable TLS1.2+, 2) prefer ECDHE-AES-GCM suites, 3) add modern EC curves (prime256v1, secp384r1), 4) test with `openssl s_client -connect ... -cipher ECDHE`, 5) avoid broad legacy policies that exclude ECDHE.

lisa-customer: Yep resolved after enabling curves and moving ECDHE suites earlier. Leaving this here for others. :thumbsup:
